source_text: Motum genitalium, id est ipsam virilitatem, sine qua non potest esse commixtio, a Deo dicimus institutam.
pass_a_gloss: The movement of the genital members, that is virility itself, without which mixing cannot be, we say was instituted by God.
pass_b_english: We say that the movement of the sexual organs—that is, the male sexual capacity itself, without which intercourse cannot take place—was instituted by God.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (Letter to Rome, words preserved in Augustine, Contra duas epistolas Pelagianorum 1); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
